newsitem.title: USA: Netanyahu rests Mideast peace hopes on Egypt.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu rests Mideast peace hopes on Egypt.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Sunday he was hopeful Egypt could encourage the Palestinians to return to the peace table, but offered no new incentive for a resumption of talks.

In an interview on Fox television, Netanyahu said he was committed to moving the peace process forward, but reiterated Israel's position to continue building a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, the contentious issue at the heart of the current crisis.
Netanyahu, who marks his first anniversary in office next Thursday, said he believed Egypt could hold the key to a resumption of the peace process between Israel and the Palestinians.
"Egypt can certainly give Palestinians the encouragement and confidence to move forward on the peace process. The position of Egypt is important.

"I hope Egypt adopts and sticks to a position that seeks moderation and seeks to have the parties come together and talk to one another. In this regard Egypt can play a very important role and I hope it will," he said.
Palestinians are pessimistic that Egypt, which became the first Arab state to make peace with Israel in a 1979 treaty, would succeed in reviving peace negotiations.
"We are not optimistic ... because of Israel's refusal to halt settlement activities," Palestinian Information Minister Yasser Abed Rabbo told Reuters in Israel.

Netanyahu denied there was any truth in a London Times newspaper report that Israeli intelligence had warned him of the potential for war with Arab states if he did not make compromises on West Bank and Jerusalem settlements.
"There is no basis for that news story," he said. "That report is not true."
Netanyahu said next week's planned summit with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak at Egypt's Sharm el-Sheikhh Red Sea resort was not based on fears of a regional war.

"We intend to make efforts to move the peace process forward regardless of what people consider the risks of war," he said. "Obviously if there is no movement for peace then the dangers of deterioration are always there and that is always uppermost in our minds.
"I intend to pursue all avenues for peace and talk to all people I can talk to in order to pursue the peace."

Palestinians want East Jerusalem as capital of a future state. They view settlement building as pre-empting final peace talks at which the city's fate is to be negotiated. They refuse to resume talks as long as construction continues.
Netanyahu called for a resumption of talks without preconditions and for the Palestinians to desist from "terrorism and violence."

"I would much rather discuss differences with the Palestinians and with Egypt without preconditions. I think it is not wise to put preconditions on talks because then we get no talks and then we just get a lot of preconditions.

"The only way we are going to move this thing forward is to talk to one another. There are things that divide us. They are quite difficult and they would better be left to the final settlement negotiations which I would hope would be launched soon.
"The pursuit of terrorism and violence should stop, both directly and indirectly as a weapon of negotiations. It's intolerable and unacceptable," he added.
